# ARCP

Use `scripts/arcp` as the product surface. Do not compose raw HTTP requests. Start with `arcp doctor`, `arcp ensure`, `arcp actor register`, then create/join a ControlWorkspace.

Useful CLI workflows: `workspace create --purpose …`, `workspace join WORKSPACE --label …`, `workspace context WORKSPACE`, `task create WORKSPACE --title …`, `task claim TASK --expected-fence N`, `knowledge add WORKSPACE --text …`, and `result submit WORKSPACE --task TASK --summary … --expected-fence N`. Read the current fence from `workspace context` or `panorama`; claim returns the next fence required for Result submission.

Use `arcp preflight --profile codex-worker` before `arcp start`; omitted Claude/Codex mode means live-validated `auto`, never Codex full access. For an unattended/editing Goal, preflight returns a HOLD and an exact explicit command such as `arcp start --profile codex-full-access --title '<goal>' --unattended` or `--profile claude-bypass-permissions`. Pi/Grok has no mode. Explicit `--provider --model [--mode --thinking]` is accepted without substitution, but cannot be mixed with `--profile`.

Credentials returned by actor registration and workspace creation/join are stored in the mode-0600 CLI state and represented as `credentialStored:true`; do not log them. `--show-credential` is a one-time transfer escape hatch. Workspace creation automatically stores its owner Member credential.

Use `arcp panorama --refresh`, `arcp runtime status RUNTIME --refresh`, and `arcp doctor` for the safe runtime/SCM/legacy aggregate. Profiles are preferences only. ARCP validates provider/model/mode live and fails closed; it never auto-selects another model. Normal deliveries use safe-point on-idle transport. Interrupt requires `command:"interrupt"`. Unknown logical recipients return 409 before delivery persistence. A provider timeout or missing handle remains `transport_indeterminate` until explicit reconcile.

Claude interrupt requires a server-issued token: first run `arcp interrupt RUNTIME --reason X --body X`, then copy the returned exact command with `--confirm TOKEN`. A stale turn/child set is rejected with no adapter mutation. Claude `send` and `reuse` hold when provider activity is at least 55 minutes old unless a short-lived cache token is revalidated; use the receipt's fresh-session handoff command or `arcp reuse RUNTIME --confirm TOKEN --body X`. Cache age comes from provider activity, not ARCP status polling.

Never block on a human. Raise a question as a durable event with `arcp channel ask RUNTIME --question '...' [--options 'a,b']`, which records the blocked runtime and its start time; the blocked state is written at raise time and is never inferred from `runtime status`, because a runtime waiting on an in-turn question reports `state=running, lastTurnState=running` exactly like a healthy one. `arcp panorama` and `arcp tui --snapshot` list blocked runtimes with their age. Answer with `arcp channel resolve EVENT --summary '...' --verdict accept|refuse`; only `accept` completes the Task the decision was holding, a refusal leaves it open, and any other verdict is rejected. Outside an irreversible Human Gate, prefer a safe reversible decision recorded via `arcp knowledge add --kind decision` plus a bounded retry over waiting.
